main_topics.reason: The user opened with severe nausea after weekly methotrexate and the whole conversation worked on fixing it.
The user asked at the start whether to quit and kept returning to avoiding that choice.
The user asked which day to take folic acid, admitted sometimes taking it on methotrexate day, and agreed to move it over several turns.
The user asked how much difference the injection makes and said they were scared of self-injecting.
The user asked whether anti-nausea medicine is safe with methotrexate after learning of it in the chat.
The user asked what to say at the appointment so as not to forget and accepted the script.
The user mentioned being a little scared of injecting in one line.
The user asked in a final question whether to keep taking it as normal for two weeks.

output.summary: A user with rheumatoid arthritis on weekly methotrexate asked whether to quit because of bad nausea. The bot explained alternatives (moving folic acid off the methotrexate day, splitting the dose, anti-nausea medicine, injection), prepared a script for the doctor, and listed warning signs. The user said they felt much better, planned changes for the weekend and agreed to continue until their appointment in two weeks.
